items.q: Universal newborn hearing programmes aim for diagnosis and intervention by which ages?
o: Diagnosis by 3 months, intervention by 6 months
items.exp: The 1-3-6 benchmark (screen by 1, diagnose by 3, intervene by 6 months) exploits early plasticity giving near normal language for many deaf infants. Waiting for speech delay forfeits this.
r: Incorrect. That misses critical language windows.
Correct. Diagnose 3 months, intervene 6 months.
Incorrect. School entry is far too late.
Incorrect. Parental detection alone misses many cases.
items.kp: One, three, six: screen, diagnose, intervene.

items.q: Commonest genetic cause of non syndromic congenital deafness is mutation in what?
items.exp: GJB2 connexin 26 gap junction mutations cause most autosomal recessive non syndromic deafness worldwide. Pendrin gives Pendred syndrome with goitre; Usher adds retinitis pigmentosa.
r: Incorrect. MITF features in Waardenburg spectrum.
Correct. Connexin 26 GJB2 is commonest.
Incorrect. Usherin causes syndromic Usher disease.
Incorrect. Pendrin is syndromic with thyroid features.
items.kp: Connexin 26 deafens most inherited non syndromic ears.

items.q: Child deafened by bacterial meningitis needs urgent implant referral because of what risk?
items.exp: Labyrinthitis ossificans can ossify cochlear turns within weeks after meningitis, blocking electrode insertion, so implant assessment is urgent. Imaging tracks ossification progression.
r: Incorrect. Wax is irrelevant canal debris.
Correct. Ossification races electrode insertion.
Incorrect. Drums usually intact in meningitic deafness.
Incorrect. Adenoids do not affect cochlea.
items.kp: Post meningitis: implant before bone fills cochlea.

items.q: Cochlear implants work by which principle?
o: Direct electrical stimulation of spiral ganglion bypassing hair cells
items.exp: External processor converts sound to electrical patterns delivered by scala tympani electrodes stimulating ganglion neurons directly, requiring an intact auditory nerve and prolonged auditory training.
r: Incorrect. Amplification is hearing aid principle.
Correct. Electrical bypass of dead hair cells.
Incorrect. Bone vibration is bone conduction device.
Incorrect. Ossiculoplasty repairs conductive chain.
items.kp: Implant talks electricity straight to the nerve.

items.q: Profound bilateral deaf infant gains best spoken language when implanted when?
o: Early, around first year where criteria met
items.exp: Auditory cortex plasticity peaks in infancy; implantation around 9 to 12 months (local criteria) with therapy gives best spoken language trajectories. Late implantation still helps but with limits.
r: Incorrect. Decade delay wastes plasticity.
Correct. Early infancy implantation is best.
Incorrect. School failure is preventable harm.
Incorrect. Adult implantation follows different indications.
items.kp: Implant early while brain wires for sound.

items.q: Bone anchored hearing device is best suited for which child?
o: Canal atresia with conductive loss and good cochlea
items.exp: Bone conduction vibrates skull bypassing atretic canal and middle ear to a normal cochlea, ideal for atresia or chronically draining ears unfit for aids. Profound sensorineural loss needs implant assessment.
r: Incorrect. Profound cochlear loss needs implant pathway.
Correct. Atresia with good cochlea suits bone device.
Incorrect. Transient glue ear gets observation.
Incorrect. Noise loss uses conventional aids if needed.
items.kp: Blocked road, good cochlea: vibrate the bone.

items.q: Pendred syndrome combines sensorineural deafness with what later feature?
items.exp: Pendrin (SLC26A4) defects cause enlarged vestibular aqueduct deafness with later euthyroid goitre in Pendred syndrome. Usher adds retinitis; Waardenburg pigment changes; osteogenesis imperfecta blue sclera.
r: Incorrect. Retinal disease marks Usher syndrome.
Correct. Goitre follows in Pendred.
Incorrect. White forelock is Waardenburg.
Incorrect. Blue sclera is osteogenesis imperfecta.

items.q: Hearing aids primarily help when which structures survive?
items.exp: Amplified sound still needs hair cells to transduce; when they are largely dead and loss profound, aids give inadequate benefit and implants are assessed. Ossicular defects may suit surgery or bone devices.
r: Incorrect. Ossicle loss can use bone routes.
Correct. Aids need surviving hair cells.
Incorrect. Facial nerve is motor, unrelated.
Incorrect. Canals govern balance, not amplification.
items.kp: No hair cells, no use amplifying: implant instead.

items.q: Congenital CMV deafness may present how after passed newborn screen?
o: Progressive or late onset sensorineural loss
items.exp: Congenital cytomegalovirus, a leading non genetic cause, can pass screening then deteriorate progressively, needing audiologic surveillance in infected infants. Early urine PCR (first weeks) proves congenital timing.
r: Incorrect. Late progression is characteristic risk.
Correct. CMV loss can arrive or worsen later.
Incorrect. Wax is transient conductive, unrelated.
Incorrect. Otosclerosis presents in young adults.
items.kp: CMV deafness can sneak in after the screen.

items.q: Parents suspect deafness despite passed newborn screen. Correct action is what?
items.exp: Parental concern is a sensitive indicator and screening misses late onset or progressive losses, so prompt diagnostic audiology (ABR and behavioural) is mandatory at any age of concern.
r: Incorrect. Reassurance risks language delay.
Correct. Test promptly on parental concern.
Incorrect. School age is too late for intervention windows.
Incorrect. Devices require measured thresholds.
items.kp: Parents worried about hearing are right until tested.
